lines.li: [us] What do you do, back home?
[them,role:trader] I trade, mostly, but I'm good at {THEIRSKILL} too.
[them,their:tribal] I am the one they call when there is {THEIRSKILL} to be done.
[them] {THEIRSKILL}, mostly, it's what I'm good at.
[us] I'd like to see that sometime.
[them] Ask nicely and you might.
[us] I'll ask very nicely.
[them] What's your work here, {COLONIST}?
[us,skill:Cooking] Cooking, and I'd like to think everyone's glad of it.
[us] {OURSKILL}, mostly, it's what I'm best at.
[them,their:tribal] A camp lives on the hands that know their work.
[them] Every place needs someone good at that.
[us] You carry yourself like someone who's been in a fight or two.
[them,their:tribal] I have hunted men as well as beasts, when I had to.
[them] More than two, and I'd rather not count them.
[us] We could use someone like you, some days.
[them] Most places could.
[us] You look like someone who knows about growing things.
[them] I've had dirt under my nails since I could walk.
[us] Then I'd take any advice going.
[them,their:tribal] Listen to the soil, and don't plant before the frogs sing.
[them] Turn the soil deep, and don't plant too early.
[us] You've a healer's hands, I'd guess.
[them,their:tribal] The plants tell me what they cure, and I listen.
[them] I've set a few bones in my time.
[us] We could use that sort of knowledge.
[them] Everyone could, sooner or later.
[them] Who does your building here?
[us] All of us, more or less.
[them] It shows, in good ways and bad.
[us] Go on, tell me the bad.
[them] Another time, when you've had a drink.
[us] Is there someone waiting for you at home?
[them] {THEIRSPOUSE}, and they'll be counting the days.
[us] Then don't keep them waiting too long.
[them,their:tribal] I'll bring a story home for every day I was gone.
[them] I won't, I've promised.
[us] Then keep it.
[us] You came with {THEIRSPOUSE}, didn't you?
[them] I did, I don't go far without them.
[us] It must make the road easier.
[them] Easier, and louder.
[us] Do you have children back home?
[them,them:smallchild] A little one, {THEIRCHILD}, who'll want to hear all about you.
[them,!them:smallchild] {THEIRCHILD}, grown now, or near enough.
[us] Do you miss them?
[them,them:smallchild] Every night, and twice on the cold ones.
[them,!them:smallchild] Less than when they were small, and more than I'd say.
[us] Give them my regards.
[us] Is that little one with you yours?
[them] {THEIRCHILD}, yes, and into everything.
[us,colony:children] Ours are the same.
[us] There's a lot here to get into.
[them] Don't I know it.
[us] Is there anyone at home for you?
[them] There was, once.
[us] I'm sorry.
[them] Thank you, it helps to hear it.
[us] If you ever want to talk about them, I'll listen.
[them] And you, {COLONIST}, anyone of your own here?
[us,us:married] {OURSPOUSE}, and I'm lucky to have them.
[us,!us:married] My child, {OURCHILD}, keeps me busy enough.
[them,them:married] Then we're both lucky.
[them] Hold on to that.
[them] No one special here for you, then?
[us] Not yet, there's always too much to do.
[them] There always will be.
[them] You keep {THEIRFAITH} too, I'm told.
[us] I do, it's good to meet another.
[them,their:lowtech] Then we say the same words at night, you and I.
[them] It makes a long road shorter, meeting your own.
[us] It does.
[them] May it watch over your people as it does over mine.
[us] Your people follow {THEIRFAITH}, don't they?
[them] We do, and you follow {OURFAITH}.
[us] Does it trouble you?
[them,them:kind] Not at all, the road has room for everyone.
[them,them:abrasive] It troubles me that you can't see the truth.
[them,!them:kind,!them:abrasive] Not so long as you don't try to change my mind.
[us] I wouldn't dream of it.
[them] Good, then we'll get along.
[us] Does your faith help, with {SITUATION}?
[them,their:tribal] We ask the spirits every night, and some nights they answer.
[them,samefaith] It helps, you'd know that yourself.
[them] It gives people something to hold on to.
[us] Something to hold on to is worth a lot.
[them] More than silver, some days.
[us] I'll remember that.
[them] Can I ask you something about {OURFAITH}?
[us] Of course.
[them] Do you ever doubt it?
[us] Some days, and then the next day I don't.
[them] Same for me with {THEIRFAITH}, if I'm honest.
[us] Then we're not so different, you and I.
[us] What do your people believe in?
[them,their:tribal] That everything has a spirit, even your walls.
[them,their:empire] In the Empire, and in our place within it.
[them,their:hightech] In what works, mostly.
[them] In getting through the day, mostly.
[us] That's a faith I understand.
[them] Most people do, sooner or later.
[us] How's trade been?
[them,town:short:food] Food sells, everything else sits.
[them,rich] Better here than most places, you're better off than most.
[them,their:tribal] We trade furs for iron, and haggle until the fire burns low.
[them] Up and down, like the weather.
[us] Let me know if you find a bargain.
[them] If I find one, I'm keeping it.
[us] What do your people want for trade?
[them,town:short:medicine] Medicine, more than anything just now.
[them,town:short:food] Grain and dried meat, as much as we can carry.
[them] Iron, salt and good cloth, the rest we make ourselves.
[us] We'll see what we can find.
[them] You don't have much to trade, do you?
[us] Not yet, give us time.
[them] I'll come back when you're rich, then.
[us] Bring a bigger cart.
[them] The Empire's goods are the finest you'll see out here.
[us] And the dearest, I'd guess.
[them] Quality has its price.
[them,deedbest:released] At home they still speak of how you let {DEEDNAME} go free.
[them] At home they still speak of the one of ours you set free.
[us] We did what was right.
[them,their:tribal] Not every people would have, and the elders know it.
[them] Not everyone would have.
[them,deedbest:tended] {DEEDNAME} came home mended, and none of us has forgotten it.
[them] You tended one of ours once, and we haven't forgotten.
[us] Anyone would have.
[them] Anyone could have, but you did.
[them] Your gifts didn't go unnoticed at home.
[us] We hoped they'd be welcome.
[them,likesus] They were, believe me.
[them] Nobody's complained, put it that way.
[them] When things were hard, your people helped, and we remember it.
[us] We'd hope someone would do the same for us.
[them,their:tribal] Then the debt is written on our hearts, not on paper.
[them] Someone will, if I have anything to say about it.
[them] You're {COLONIST}, aren't you, the one they talk about at home?
[us] I hope it's nothing bad.
[them,byyou:freed] You set one of ours free, nobody forgets that.
[them,byyou:tended] You tended one of ours, nobody forgets that.
[them,byyou:helped] You did right by one of ours, nobody forgets that.
[us] It was nothing, really.
[them] It wasn't nothing to us.
[them] Is {FRIEND} about?
[us] Somewhere, why do you ask?
[them] {FRIEND} did right by my people once, and they ask after them at home.
[us] I'll pass that on.
[them] Do, it would mean something to them.
[them,wrongbest:killed] {WRONGNAME} had family, and they remember.
[them,wrongbest:captured] Some at home still talk about {WRONGNAME} being taken.
[them] Some at home still hold a grudge against your people.
[us] I'd hoped that was behind us.
[them] Time helps, and so does good company.
[them] You owe us one, you know.
[us] We haven't forgotten.
[them,their:empire] The Empire keeps careful accounts.
[them] Good, I'll hold you to it one day.
[them] Have you kept up what I showed you?
[us,trait:Lazy] When I find the time.
[us] Every day I can.
[them] Good, it only sticks if you use it.
[them] I've been thinking about our bout.
[us] Thinking about a rematch?
[them] Thinking I'll win it.
[them] I haven't forgotten what you said to me.
[us,trait:Kind] I'm sorry, I shouldn't have said it.
[us] I meant every word.
[us] What would you do, if you could do anything?
[them,their:tribal] Walk to the edge of the world and see what's there.
[them,role:trader] Sell everything I own and buy a boat.
[them] Settle somewhere quiet and grow old.
[us] That doesn't sound so bad.
[them] And you?
[us] Ask me again when I've had time to think.
[us] You must have seen a lot of changes.
[them,them:kind] More than I can count, and some of them for the better.
[them,them:abrasive] More than I can count, and most of them for the worse.
[them,!them:kind,!them:abrasive] More than I can count, good and bad.
[us] Tell me one sometime.
[them] Sit down, then, it's a long one.
[us] I've got all evening.
[us] You're hurt, does it need seeing to?
[them] It's mending, thank you.
[us] Ask if it gets worse.
[them] You're moving like it hurts.
[us] It does, but I'll live.
[them,their:tribal] Pain is a teacher with a loud voice.
[them] Don't push it.
[them] I always look forward to coming here, you know.
[us] And we always look forward to you coming.
[them,their:tribal] Then our paths are tied, you and I.
[them] Good, then I'll keep coming.
[them] Do you know what my people say about yours?
[us] Do I want to?
[them,their:tribal] That you build walls to keep the sky out.
[them] That you work too hard and sleep too little.
[us] They're not wrong.
[them] Your sky's clearer than ours.
[us] Fewer fires, maybe.
[them,their:tribal] My grandmother named every one of those stars.
[them] I could look at it all night.
